record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: Is there an algorithm that decides whether two subshifts of finite type are topologically conjugate by homeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Question 1.9 (Foreman). Is there an algorithm for determining whether two subshifts of finite type are conjugate by homeomorphisms?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a finite set of finite words over $A$. The (two-sided) subshift of finite type determined by $\mathcal{F}$ is the set
$$X_{\mathcal F}=\{x\in A^{\mathbb Z}: \text{no word from }\mathcal F\text{ occurs in }x\},$$
equipped with the product topology and the shift map $\sigma:X_{\mathcal F}\to X_{\mathcal F}$ defined by $(\sigma x)_n=x_{n+1}$. Two such subshifts $(X,\sigma_X)$ and $(Y,\sigma_Y)$ are said to be topologically conjugate if there exists a homeomorphism $h:X\to Y$ with $h\circ\sigma_X=\sigma_Y\circ h$.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm which, given as input two finite presentations (i.e., the alphabets $A,B$ and finite forbidden-word lists $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$) of subshifts of finite type $X_{\mathcal F}\subseteq A^{\mathbb Z}$ and $X_{\mathcal G}\subseteq B^{\mathbb Z}$, decides whether $X_{\mathcal F}$ and $X_{\mathcal G}$ are topologically conjugate?
artifact.category_tag: Symbolic dynamics / subshifts of finite type
artifact.status_search_result: The decidability of topological conjugacy for two-sided one-dimensional subshifts of finite type is a long-standing open problem in symbolic dynamics, prominently listed in Boyle's open-problems survey. Partial results exist: conjugacy is decidable for one-sided SFTs and for tree-shifts of finite type, and "direct conjugacy" via N-block presentations is decidable; the multidimensional case has hardness results. The general two-sided question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems in Symbolic Dynamics (Boyle)
status_evidence.snippet: There are many open decidability problems, including the question of whether there exists a decision procedure for determining when SFTs are topologically conjugate.
status_evidence.claim: Decidability of conjugacy of SFTs is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Decidability of Conjugacy of Tree-Shifts of Finite Type
status_evidence.snippet: Conjugacy is decidable for tree-shifts of finite type, closer to one-sided shifts than two-sided ones.
status_evidence.claim: Decidability is known in related/special cases but not the general two-sided case.

status_evidence.title: N-block presentations and decidability of direct conjugacy between SFTs
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of N,M such that the N-block presentation of X is similar to the M-block presentation of Y (which implies conjugacy) is decidable.
status_evidence.claim: Partial decidability results exist for direct conjugacy via block presentations.
